name: Practice advance, undo, and complete
userOutcome: User advances beads by whole-screen tap, undoes one step if needed, and reaches a distinct completion state exactly once at the target count. The completion event must be perceptibly distinguishable from an ordinary per-bead tick through haptics and/or tone, without requiring the user to look at the screen — including when the ringer is silenced, since the completion tone intentionally uses the .ambient audio category and the haptic alone must then carry the signal.
productionDataSource: Live PracticeController + JapaEngine state; preferences target count; selected mantra labels only (does not affect count).
errorBehavior: Invalid advances when already complete return alreadyComplete and do not re-fire completion side effects. Undo floors at 0. Persistence failures must not silently invent progress.
accessibilityRequirements: Advance and undo are accessible actions
Progress is available to VoiceOver without requiring vision
Respect reduce motion where animation is cosmetic
Completion must be signaled through a haptic pattern and/or tone that is distinguishable from the ordinary per-bead tick pattern, so an eyes-free user can tell progress from completion by feel alone
prohibitedBehavior: Do not use undisclosed sample data in production history
Do not fire completion haptic/tone more than once per round
Do not require looking at the screen to advance
Do not make the completion haptic pattern identical to (indistinguishable from) the per-bead tick pattern
Do not let the silent-switch/muted case leave the user with no perceptible completion signal at all — the haptic must carry the signal when the tone is suppressed
acceptanceTests: PracticeFlowTests — complete records history and clears resumable
JapaUITests — tap advance/undo and reach completion
verificationGaps: No automated test spies on HapticFeedback/TonePlaying to verify that advance() calls tick() while only the target-reaching advance() calls completion(), or that tone.play() fires on completion when the preference is enabled. Every existing test injects NoopHaptics/NoopTone or never inspects them (confirmed by source audit, 2026-07-17).
No acceptance test models the muted/silent-switch scenario to confirm the haptic-only fallback actually delivers a distinguishable completion signal.
Perceptual distinctness of tick vs. completion haptic patterns on physical hardware is unvalidated — tracked as docs/BUGS.md B-HAPT, device-only verification, Simulator insufficient.
